newsitem.title: UK: London will remain key insurance market - industry.
newsitem.headline: London will remain key insurance market - industry.

text.p: London will retain its position as an important hub of the insurance industry, despite the recent difficulties experienced by Lloyds of London, the chairman of industry association LIRMA said.

"London is not dead, it is doing well and will continue to do so provided its constituents do not think parochially and work together to increase the size of the cake," Philip Marcell said in a speech delivered in New York.
LIRMA, the London International Insurance and Reinsurance Market Association, represents many of the international insurers and reinsurers operating in London.

Marcell, who is also chairman of Unionamerica Insurance Company Ltd, was addressing a Mealey's conference on 'First Reactions to the New Reinsurance Market.' A copy of his speech was made available in London.

"With Lloyd's reconstruction and renewal now moving ahead, and the desire of the London market as a whole to co-operate in a way so as to produce the best framework for the production and underwriting business at the lowest cost, I see no reason why London should not continue to be a key market for wholesale insurance and reinsurance in the future," he said.
Modern systems, ease of access, London's overall infrastructure and geographical concentration were the benefits offered to insurers by the London market, he added.
However, Marcell said that the global market had changed and the expansion of reinsurance companies in Europe, the U.S. and particularly Bermuda could not be ignored.
"(Bermuda) does produce significant amounts of capacity for what I would call commodity products. We also see increased capacity in regional markets in Asia and elsewhere."

"London cannot expect to be as dominant as in the past; but I do think it will continue to be dominant in speciality lines, particularly where real innovation is called for, rather than simply price cutting."
Marcell said he did not expect capital markets to take over the reinsurance industry, which some observers believe will not be able to cope with increasing demand.
"While I accept that there might be timing gaps, the reinsurance industry has always managed to increase its capacity to cope with demand."
He also said he saw a future for niche and regional reinsurers alongside the industry giants.
"You can survive at lower levels of capital if you are a specialist company with a history of expertise and can focus your writings accordingly."
Marcell put the minimum capital requirements of a niche reinsurer at $125-$500 million, but added that regional companies in developing markets could exist with a lower capital base.
